# Jewel Labs

> Hard tech for the diamond trade.

## What we build

The first ML automated desk diamond grader: software and a portable scanning machine
that fits on a trading desk and travels in a carry-on. A polished
stone is scanned under controlled imaging, lighting and sensing conditions. The
software reads the stone's visual and sensor signature, writes a structured
fingerprint record, and converts that into an industry-aligned grade.

The system grades across every category that determines value: cut, colour, clarity,
carat, proportions, fluorescence, symmetry, polish, and the other optical and
material signals that separate a natural stone from a grown one.

The software can be sold on its own to businesses that already run imaging
workflows. The machine adds the controlled conditions, the data capture and the
throughput.

## How it works

1. Load. The stone drops into a sealed chamber, where outside light never reaches it.
2. Light. Calibrated arrays cycle through brightfield, darkfield and raking light. A 365 nm pass reads fluorescence.
3. Measure. Structured light maps the facets. A load cell takes carat weight on the same stage.
4. Separate. A spectrometer reads the optical signature, which is what tells natural from CVD and HPHT.
5. Grade. The model assigns every category that carries price, each with a confidence value.
6. Record. A fingerprint record is written, and everything downstream is built from it.

## Throughput

A human grader evaluates one stone at a time and a high volume parcel can take days.
The machine is designed for parallel scanning at a target throughput of thousands of
diamonds per hour, turning grading from a manual bottleneck into an automated data
pipeline.

## The layer above

A second machine learning layer reads the records and assembles the filing, including
the EU due diligence statement, moving documents between houses and their agents. If a
stone's paperwork and its scan disagree, it blocks on the desk instead of at the border.
